speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I’m Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition better, could you describe the nature of your right flank pain and when the hematuria started?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of kidney stones, and are you currently experiencing fever or chills?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any nausea or vomiting along with the pain, and does the pain radiate toward your groin? Also, have you noticed any changes in your urinary frequency or urgency?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history except noted recurrent urinary tract infections. No history of renal dialysis or known genetic diseases. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works in an office setting.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a family history of kidney stones or polycystic kidney disease? I would like to correlate your symptoms with imaging findings. REQUEST TEST: CT_Urinary_Tract

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CT scan is normal, I need to rule out other causes of hematuria. Do you have any pain or burning during urination, and have you noticed any changes in the color of your urine other than blood, such as it becoming foamy or cloudy?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dysuria, or any recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CT is normal and infectious symptoms are absent, I suspect a glomerular source for the hematuria. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis_Microscopy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis Microscopy shows RBCs: Too numerous to count, WBCs: 10-20 /HPF, Leukocyte Esterase: Positive, Nitrites: Negative

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive leukocyte esterase and presence of white blood cells despite negative nitrites suggest sterile pyuria, which raises suspicion for atypical organisms like *Chlamydia* or early tuberculosis. Given your history of recurrent UTIs and persistent flank pain, I need to rule out an occult infection or inflammatory condition. REQUEST TEST: Urine_Culture_and_Sensitivity

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the sterile pyuria and negative standard workup, I suspect a structural abnormality like a small ureteral stone or early malignancy that the CT may have missed. REQUEST TEST: Renal_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: All structural and infectious causes have been ruled out by normal imaging and cultures, leaving a glomerular origin as the most likely diagnosis for your sterile pyuria and hematuria. DIAGNOSIS READY: IgA Nephropathy
